questions: If multiple positions (a,b) satisfy the condition, should any valid pair be output or is there a required tie‑breaking rule (e.g., smallest a, then smallest b)?
Are the indices a and b 1‑based as described, and should they be printed exactly as those 1‑based values?
Must the program output a pair even when no occurrence of T exists in S, and if so, what should be printed in that case?
Is the input guaranteed to contain exactly N lines for S followed by exactly M lines for T, with no extra whitespace or blank lines?
Are there any limits on line length or trailing spaces in the input lines, and should trailing spaces be ignored?
Should the program treat the characters '.' and '#' case‑sensitively, i.e., are only those two exact characters allowed?
Is it allowed for N and M to be equal (so S and T are the same size), and in that case should the answer be (1,1) if the grids match?
Are there any constraints on the time or memory limits that could affect the choice of algorithm, or are typical competitive‑programming limits assumed?

inline_prompts: You are given an N \times N grid S and an M \times M grid T. The cell at the i-th row from the top and the j-th column from the left is denoted by (i,j). The colors of the cells in S and T are represented by N^2 characters S_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq N) and M^2 characters T_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq M), respectively. In grid S, cell (i,j) is white if S_{i,j} is ., and black if S_{i,j} is #. The same applies for grid T. Find T within S. More precisely, output integers a and b (1 \leq a,b \leq N-M+1) that satisfy the following condition: There is exactly one valid pair (a,b); print only that one, no tie-break rule needed. S_{a+i-1,b+j-1} = T_{i,j} for every i,j (1\leq i,j \leq M). Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M S_{1,1}S_{1,2}\dots S_{1,N} S_{2,1}S_{2,2}\dots S_{2,N} \vdots S_{N,1}S_{N,2}\dots S_{N,N} T_{1,1}T_{1,2}\dots T_{1,M} T_{2,1}T_{2,2}\dots T_{2,M} \vdots T_{M,1}T_{M,2}\dots T_{M,M} Output Print a and b in this order, separated by a space on one line. Constraints 1 \leq M \leq N \leq 50 N and M are integers. Each of S_{i,j} and T_{i,j} is . or #.
